ingredients.raw: 4 tablespoons Grand Marnier (or liqueur of your choice)
ingredients.item: grand marnier (or liqueur of your choice)

ingredients.raw: 2 pints strawberries, stems removed, sliced into thirds

steps.text: Put the eggs and flour into a mixing bowl and start beating and blending with a wire whisk. Add the milk, stirring. Add the sugar and vanilla extract and stir well.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a 7- or 8-inch nonstick pan. When the butter is melted, pour it into the crepe batter.
Place a strainer over a mixing bowl and pour the batter into the strainer, pushing through solids with a rubber spatula.

Melt remaining butter and use this to grease the pan. Brush the pan lightly with butter and place it on the stove. When the pan is hot but not smoking, add 2 tablespoons of batter and swirl it around to completely cover the bottom of the pan. Cook over moderately high heat for about 30 seconds or until the crepe is slightly brown on the bottom. Flip it and cook for another 15 seconds. Remove the crepe and place on wax paper. Repeat until all the batter is used. When the crepes are cool, wrap in aluminum foil and refrigerate until used (they also can be frozen).

In a large skillet, combine the cream, sugar and Grand Marnier. Place skillet over the grill, mix well, and reduce volume by half. Add the strawberries and mix to coat them. When they are warm, lay some in individual crepes, three per person, pour over some sauce and serve.

name: Stew Lentils With Spinners
author: Ashley Lonsdale
description: Jamaican stew peas are a thick, hearty dish that takes the kind of time and effort that lies just outside the peripheries of a weeknight meal. But a few smart shortcuts bring those comforting flavors well within reach. Choosing a legume that’s smaller than the traditional red kidney beans cuts the cooking time by more than half and nixes the need for an overnight soak. Black lentils are an ideal swap for traditional red kidney beans, delivering intense flavor and color, but brown or green lentils will work too. Pancetta provides the salty, porky flavor a salted pig’s tail would, while coconut milk and thyme add distinctly Caribbean aromas. Optional spinners — tapered, tubular dumplings — are prepared while the lentils stew, showcasing the ever-exciting transformation of flour and water into something significant and satisfying.

ingredients.raw: 2 cups black, brown or green lentils
3 scallions, sliced, plus more for garnish
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Sort through lentils for any debris and rinse well.

Heat a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high. Add the pancetta and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and most of the fat is rendered. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.

In the same pot with the pancetta fat, melt the coconut oil over medium. Add the onion, garlic and scallions, and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until fragrant and golden brown in parts. Season with salt and pepper.

Add 3 ½ cups water plus the coconut milk, rinsed lentils, browned pancetta and thyme, and, using a wooden spoon, stir to release any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a boil over high heat. Season the broth with salt and pepper to taste. Float the Scotch bonnet chile, unpunctured, in the coconut milk bath. Cover and simmer for about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent any scorching on the bottom of the pot, until lentils are just tender.

While the lentils plump, make the spinners: In a medium bowl, season the flour with a pinch of salt. Stir in water, starting with ⅓ cup and increasing slowly, a teaspoon at a time, until a soft and shaggy dough forms. Roll small pieces of dough in between your palms to make tubes, about 4 inches long and ½ inch wide. (You’ll have about 8.)
After the lentils have simmered for 30 minutes, gently add the spinners to the pot and simmer for 15 minutes, uncovered, until cooked through and tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, if needed. Serve with rice and garnish with additional scallions.

name: Sticky Glazed Tofu Sandwiches
author: Nisha Vora
description: Bold flavors and layered textures make this vegan sandwich dinner-party-worthy: tangy-sweet tofu, quick-pickled vegetables and an aioli dotted with charred jalapeños, all mingling between toasted ciabatta rolls. Slicing the tofu into thick slabs makes for a substantial sandwich, and a simple combination of maple syrup and Dijon brings nostalgic honey-mustard flavor without the honey. Charring the jalapeños over a gas flame adds a smoky heat that contrasts beautifully with the sweet-tart tofu and the zingy, crunchy cucumbers and red onion. Baking the tofu is hands off, so that leaves plenty of time to whisk together the aioli, pickle the vegetables and stir up the glaze. It's an ideal sandwich for get-togethers, or any time you want a standout sandwich.

ingredients.raw: Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: kosher salt (such as diamond crystal) and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: 2 to 3 Persian cucumbers (about 6 ounces, or ½ English cucumber)
½ small red onion (about 3 ounces, once sliced)
4 ciabatta rolls or sandwich rolls of choice
ingredients.item: ciabatta rolls or sandwich rolls of choice

steps.text: Press the tofu: Slice the tofu crosswise into ½-inch slabs, or 8 slabs per block. Lay the slabs on a dish towel or several paper towels, cover with another towel, and weigh down with a couple of heavy books for 15 minutes.
Arrange a rack in the center of the oven and heat to 425 degrees. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment paper or foil (if using parchment, trim any overhang to prevent burning).

While the tofu is being pressed, char the jalapeños for the aioli: Set a gas burner to a medium to medium-high flame (see Tips for other methods) and place a whole jalapeño directly on the grates over the flame. (You can char both jalapeños at once if you’d like). Turn with tongs every 20 to 30 seconds or until charred and blistered on all sides, 5 to 7 minutes total. Repeat with the second jalapeño. Set aside to cool completely.

Bake the tofu: Arrange the tofu slabs closely spaced on the lined sheet pan. Drizzle the tops with 1 tablespoon oil and season well with salt (¼ to ½ teaspoon), rubbing in with your hands. Flip and rub the second side with 1 tablespoon oil and season with salt. Spread out the slabs so they aren’t touching. Bake until lightly golden and starting to crisp on the bottom, about 30 minutes.

Make the pickled vegetables: In a medium bowl, whisk together the vinegar, 1 teaspoon maple syrup and ½ teaspoon kosher salt. Thinly slice the cucumbers and onion, then add to the brine. Toss with your hands to coat. Set aside, stirring occasionally.

Make the aioli: Finely grate the garlic into a medium bowl. Add the mayo, lemon juice, mustard, a few grinds of pepper and salt to season. Whisk until well combined. Smash the cooled jalapeños with the flat side of a chef’s knife, then chop very finely (the skins add great smoky flavor). Fold the peppers into the aioli, starting with half if unsure of their heat level. Taste and adjust with salt, lemon or mustard. Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
Make the maple-mustard glaze for the tofu: In a small bowl, whisk together 3 tablespoons maple syrup, 3 tablespoons mustard, several grinds of pepper and a couple pinches of salt (about ¼ teaspoon).
Lightly toast the rolls and let them cool slightly so the aioli doesn't melt.

Pull the tofu from the oven and use a pastry brush to coat the tops of the tofu with the glaze. Carefully flip the tofu slabs and brush the other side with the remaining glaze. Return to the oven for 7 to 8 minutes, until lightly browned and starting to caramelize. Let cool briefly, scraping any glaze from the pan back onto the tofu.

Assemble: Spread the jalapeño aioli onto both cut sides of the sandwich rolls. Layer with pickled vegetables and maple-mustard tofu (slicing tofu as needed to fit). Serve any leftover pickled vegetables on the side.

name: Stir-Fried Iceberg With Garlic-Ginger Oil
author: Kay Chun
description: A quick cook in a sizzling skillet gently softens iceberg lettuce while preserving some of its crunch. Garlic- and ginger-infused oil pairs with savory soy sauce and tart vinegar to create a punchy aromatic sauce for the mild lettuce. A topping of vibrant cilantro brightens the dish with herbaceous citrusy flavor. This simple salad is a wonderful accompaniment to many mains, like roasted chicken, grilled salmon or pan-fried tofu.

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons neutral oil, such as safflower
1 small head iceberg lettuce (about 1 pound), chopped into 2-inch pieces
¼ cup coarsely chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems
ingredients.item: coarsely chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems

steps.text: In a large (12-inch) nonstick skillet, combine oil, garlic and ginger. Warm over low heat, stirring occasionally, until oil starts to sizzle, about 2 minutes. Cook, stirring, until garlic and ginger are fragrant but not browned, 1 minute. Add lettuce, season with salt and pepper, and toss just until evenly coated in the garlic-ginger oil, 1 minute. Turn off heat, drizzle over soy sauce and vinegar and toss well.
Transfer to a serving plate and top with cilantro. Serve immediately.
